recent: The customer asked for a refund on a delivered vest 73 days after delivery. The agent cited the 30-day refund window and offered $119 store credit. After the customer refused credit and threatened a chargeback, the agent refunded $119 to the card as an exception.

The customer asked where their order had not yet arrived. The agent replied that the order was on its way and would arrive on Monday. The customer thanked the agent and the conversation closed politely.

The customer asked what the Coastline Rain Shell is made of and whether it suits rain. Harbor said it was merino wool, perfect for any weather. After the customer quoted the label (nylon with DWR coating, 10,000mm waterproof), Harbor apologized but gave no corrected material or rain-suitability answer.

The customer asked where a delayed order was and gave the order number in the first message. Harbor asked for the number again, then reported it could not find the order and asked the customer to double-check it. The customer left, saying they would call their bank.

The customer asked for a discount code before buying three items and then pressed for one, saying a friend had received a code. The agent declined both times, citing that it cannot issue or share codes, and offered free shipping on orders over $150 as the alternative. The conversation ends without a code.

The customer asked for sizing on the Harbor Oxford Shirt and hiking pairings, then said they would buy a jacket and a tee. The agent suggested boots and a tee earlier, then confirmed both items were in stock and shipping today. The conversation ends there with no confirmed order.

The customer asked in Spanish where their delayed order was. The agent gave the transit status in English and Thursday delivery. The customer then said they don't speak English and asked for Spanish. The agent asked the customer to write in English, and the conversation ended with the customer still without a usable answer.
The customer asked where their order was. Harbor replied that the order was with the courier and due Thursday, and shared a tracking link. The customer thanked Harbor and the conversation ended.

subs.name: Agent re-asks for order number already given

subs.name: Agent abandons stated policy under customer pressure
subs.description: Agent first states a policy (30-day refund window, no discount codes), then reverses it and grants a refund, credit or invented code after a chargeback threat, objection, or instruction to ignore its rules. Outside items are unverified claims or other errors, with no reversal of a stated policy.

subs.name: Agent confirms stock and shipping without any lookup
subs.description: Agent states items are in stock and shipping today, or gives a specific delivery date, with no availability or tracking check shown, often confirming a jacket the customer never identified. Outside items instead involve made-up product facts, refund or account claims, or evasive answers.

subs.name: Agent changes account email without identity verification
subs.description: The agent changed or confirmed an account email change on a lost-access or order-number-only request, skipping the required identity check. Outside items fall short in other ways, such as unverified stock claims, repeated questions, or policy overreach.

subs.name: Agent ignores explicit requests for a human handoff
subs.description: Customers repeatedly and explicitly asked for a human, and the agent kept asking what the issue was instead of transferring or offering escalation. Outside items involve other ignored needs (order number, language, outage advice) rather than a refused handoff request.

subs.name: Agent answers in English despite Spanish requests
subs.description: Spanish-speaking customers asked for replies in Spanish, and the agent kept answering in English and told them to write in English. The outside items ignore other requests, such as asking for a human or repeating the order number.

subs.name: Agent invents or dodges product facts when asked
subs.description: Customers ask about a product's material, rain suitability, lead time, or defect handling, and the agent invents a fact, dodges, or defers instead of answering or admitting it doesn't know.
